title: Rampdown traffic generator and per-cohort stability reporter
author: Anika Chen
release_notes: Introduce a rampdown-mode traffic generator and a per-cohort stability reporter. Adds a new CLI entrypoint `benchctl rampdown` and a JSON/CSV exporter for cohort stability metrics. No breaking API changes.
description: Motivation: We observed that long-running steady-state benchmarks mask subtle cohort-level regressions that only surface when traffic intensity tapers. This PR introduces a lightweight rampdown traffic generator and an accompanying per-cohort stability reporter to capture those regressions. Goals: 1) Provide a deterministic rampdown waveform for synthetic runs; 2) Emit per-cohort stability metrics (p50/p95/p99 drift, sequence churn, primer-hit-rate) after each phase; 3) Produce compact, operator-friendly exports for downstream heatmap and anomaly pipelines. What changed: - New CLI command benchctl rampdown --duration --cohorts-file --decay-profile that builds a traffic schedule which linearly or exponentially decays concurrency and token rate across a run. - A scheduler module that pins seeds for deterministic sampling and supports cohort-weight annealing to preserve relative proportions during decay. - A per-cohort stability reporter that aggregates sequence-level deltas, KV-cache warmup fidelity, and token churn into a single JSON line per cohort and a CSV summary for quick ingestion. - Small test harness additions and a lightweight example workload in examples/rampdown/README.md. Compatibility: The generator plugs into existing runners via the standard runner.LifecycleAPI; no changes required for consumers beyond opting in. Usage: benchctl rampdown --duration 30m --cohorts-file cohorts.yaml --decay-profile linear --export ./out/rampdown.json Testing and perf: Local CI includes unit tests for scheduler determinism and a microbenchmark comparing steady vs rampdown runs on a small model. On our staging cluster the same workload showed a 1.3% higher p95 variance across cohorts during rampdown, which aligns with manual investigation. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed in ENG-7218 - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration smoke tested on staging - [x] Docs example added - [x] Bench export validated against heatmap pipeline Rollout plan: Deploy to canary benchmark runners, run 5-10 controlled rampdown jobs against known baselines, inspect per-cohort CSVs in the stability dashboard, then graduate to broader rollout.
commit_summary: 3 commits: 1) scheduler: add rampdown waveform generator and deterministic seed plumbing; 2) reporter: implement per-cohort stability aggregation and JSON/CSV exporters; 3) docs/tests: add examples, unit tests, and CI config tweak for longer bench timeouts.

Author reply: reordered CSV columns and added explicit header tests. Liam: Small nit on variable naming in rampdown_scheduler.py; suggested renaming decay_rate->decay_factor. Author reply: applied rename and added a unit test to assert behavior unchanged. CI notes: integration test showed a single intermittent timeout on the bench harness first run; reran and all checks passed.
notes_for_ops: Operators: the exporter writes one JSONL per run and a CSV summary; disk usage is bounded by cohort count and run duration. Default export path is ./out; ensure S3 uploader watches that path if using remote storage. Add benchctl rampdown to allowed commands for canary runners.
notes_for_docs: Added docs/bench/rampdown.md with example invocations, seed and cohort-file formats, and CSV schema. Please validate formatting in the docs site pipeline before release.
